instructions: Cut the 1.5 lbs of chicken thighs into 1-inch pieces, pat them dry with paper towels, and transfer them into a large bowl.

Grate 3 of the garlic cloves and the 1 tbsp of ginger into the bowl. Cut the lemon in half and squeeze one half over the chicken, about 2 tbsp. Add 1 tbsp of the oil, 1 tsp of the salt, the pepper, the turmeric, 1 tsp of the coriander, 1/2 tsp of the cumin and 1 tsp of the chili powder. Toss until every piece is coated, and let it sit for 10 minutes while you chop.

Slice the onions thinly and chop the tomatoes. Mince the 2 remaining garlic cloves. Chop 1/4 cup of the cilantro. Slice the green chilies into a small bowl for the table, and cut the other lemon half into wedges.

Heat a 12-inch skillet over medium-high for a minute, then add 2 tbsp of the oil. Lay the chicken in a single layer and leave it alone for 3 minutes, until the underside is deep brown and lets go of the pan. Flip the pieces and brown the other side for 3 minutes. It won't be cooked through yet. Transfer the chicken to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium and add the last 1 tbsp of oil, then the onions. Cook, stirring, for 3 minutes, until soft and starting to brown. Add the minced garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Stir in the remaining 1 tsp of coriander, the remaining 1/2 tsp of cumin and the remaining 1/2 tsp of chili powder. Cook for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, the remaining 3/4 tsp of salt and 1/4 cup of water. Scrape up the browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Cook for 3 minutes, until the tomatoes break down into a thick sauce.

Return the chicken and any juices to the pan. Stir, cover, and cook over medium-low for 5 minutes. You're cooking the chicken to 175°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check a thick piece. No thermometer? Cut one open: it's done when there's no pink left.
Take the pan off the heat. Stir in the garam masala and the chopped cilantro.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a squeeze of the lemon wedges.
Serve with rice and the lemon wedges. Put the sliced green chilies on the table for the adults.
method_notes: Nish Kitchen's tawa chicken is the only version found with a real number of ratings: it browns bite-size chicken in a hot pan, then cooks it down with onion, tomato, ginger, green chili and cilantro. Sinfully Spicy sears first, blooms ground spices and finishes with a ground whole-spice tawa masala and a pat of butter, and Sugar Spice & More adds garam masala and green chili at the end. The lead uses a bought tandoori paste, which can contain yogurt, so a spice paste of lemon, garlic, ginger, oil and ground spices stands in for it, and oil replaces the butter, so the dish stays dairy-free and gluten-free. The green chilies move to the table to keep the pan mild.
